## Summary of Findings

**CHK-0146 / CHK-0147 / CHK-0148 (PROP-W5B14-18) — CONFIRMED VULNERABILITY (Medium Severity)**

The critical finding is that `ReconstructDataColumnSidecars` in `/home/gohan/runners/security-agent-2/_work/security-agent/security-agent/target_workspace/beacon-chain/core/peerdas/reconstruction.go` (lines 108-119) stamps reconstructed sidecars with `blocks.NewVerifiedRODataColumn()` without calling `kzg.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch` on the recovered cells. The comment at line 108 ("Input sidecars are verified, and we reconstructed ourselves the missing sidecars. As a consequence, reconstructed sidecars are also verified.") is an incorrect logical deduction — it is only valid if `ckzg4844.RecoverCellsAndKZGProofs` is trusted completely and unconditionally. The `VerifiedRODataColumn` type is documented in `rodatacolumn.go` as representing "full verification (block sig, inclusion proof, commitment check)" — but commitment check is bypassed for reconstructed columns. The reconstructed columns are subsequently saved to persistent storage (`dataColumnStorage.Save`) and broadcast to peers (`broadcastMissingDataColumnSidecars`), making this a data-poisoning risk if the C library produces incorrect-but-non-error output. The fix infrastructure already exists: `VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs` in `p2p_interface.go` performs exactly the needed batch KZG proof verification and is already used for all network-received columns.

**CHK-0149 / CHK-0150 (PROP-W5B14-19) — OUT OF SCOPE**

The functions `recover_polynomialcoeff` and the constant `PRIMITIVE_ROOT_OF_UNITY` referenced in these checks do not exist in the Go codebase. All polynomial arithmetic is delegated to the `ckzg4844` C library. Error propagation from the C library is correctly implemented in Go. These checks belong to an audit of the `ethereum/c-kzg-4844` library, not this Prysm Go repository.

## Summary of Findings

**CHK-0146 / CHK-0147 / CHK-0148 (PROP-W5B14-18) — CONFIRMED VULNERABILITY (Medium Severity)**

The critical finding is that `ReconstructDataColumnSidecars` in `/home/gohan/runners/security-agent-2/_work/security-agent/security-agent/target_workspace/beacon-chain/core/peerdas/reconstruction.go` (lines 108-119) stamps reconstructed sidecars with `blocks.NewVerifiedRODataColumn()` without calling `kzg.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch` on the recovered cells. The comment at line 108 ("Input sidecars are verified, and we reconstructed ourselves the missing sidecars. As a consequence, reconstructed sidecars are also verified.") is an incorrect logical deduction — it is only valid if `ckzg4844.RecoverCellsAndKZGProofs` is trusted completely and unconditionally. The `VerifiedRODataColumn` type is documented in `rodatacolumn.go` as representing "full verification (block sig, inclusion proof, commitment check)" — but commitment check is bypassed for reconstructed columns. The reconstructed columns are subsequently saved to persistent storage (`dataColumnStorage.Save`) and broadcast to peers (`broadcastMissingDataColumnSidecars`), making this a data-poisoning risk if the C library produces incorrect-but-non-error output. The fix infrastructure already exists: `VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs` in `p2p_interface.go` performs exactly the needed batch KZG proof verification and is already used for all network-received columns.

**CHK-0149 / CHK-0150 (PROP-W5B14-19) — OUT OF SCOPE**

The functions `recover_polynomialcoeff` and the constant `PRIMITIVE_ROOT_OF_UNITY` referenced in these checks do not exist in the Go codebase. All polynomial arithmetic is delegated to the `ckzg4844` C library. Error propagation from the C library is correctly implemented in Go. These checks belong to an audit of the `ethereum/c-kzg-4844` library, not this Prysm Go repository.
